function: Joint ISAC transmit beamforming and power allocation at the RSU, maximizing communication sum-rate under CRLB sensing-accuracy constraints, from current sensing state (p. 6-7).
system: Massive MIMO ULA RSU with 32 transmit and 32 receive antennas serving three single-antenna vehicles at 30 GHz; no RIS (p. 3, p. 10).
method: Reinforcement learning: actor-critic PPO whose actor and critic are spiking neural networks (LIF neurons, three fully connected layers, 128 hidden), trained by interaction with a simulated environment (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator, no dataset: three vehicles on a straight road, path-loss exponent model, radar echo with Doppler and delay; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured data (p. 4-5, p. 10).
test_conditions: Trained and tested in one simulated scenario (three vehicles, 32 antennas, 100 slots); only maximum transmit power is swept, 0 to 40 dBm (p. 10, p. 12).
baselines: Learned: PPO, DDPG, DQN. Non-learned: Random scheme (p. 11).
metrics: Training reward, energy per training episode and per inference action, achievable sum-rate versus time and maximum power, RMSE of angle and distance (p. 11-13).
complexity: FLOPs-based energy with formulas (p. 11); training 5.15 times lower than PPO/DDPG, 2.58 times lower than DQN; inference 6.87 to 7.125 times lower (p. 3, p. 12).
q1_support: p. 10: "We consider a scenario with three vehicles (i.e., K = 3), each equipped with a single antenna, driving along a straight road." Custom simulator with its own path-loss and echo model (p. 4-5); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is named.
q2_support: p. 12: "we vary the maximum transmit power at the RSU" is only a power sweep; the single scenario of p. 10 (K = 3, 32 antennas) is used throughout, and no new scenario, vehicle count, or antenna count is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [36], Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) [45], DQN [30], and Random scheme." p. 12: "outperforming baseline algorithms such as PPO, DDPG, DQN, and Random allocation" on sum-rate; p. 13: RMSE reductions versus DQN and Random.
q4_support: p. 11: "the total number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is used to quantify the computational workload during training and inference"; FLOPs formulas and energy ratios (5.15 times in training, p. 12). Cost is given as FLOPs-derived energy, not raw FLOPs counts.
q5_support: p. 10: "We consider a scenario with three vehicles (i.e., K = 3)" shows data come from a custom simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset (the text ends at p. 13 with the conclusion and references).
notes: ISAC beamforming and power allocation for V2X, so area 5. The PDF is the arXiv v2 preprint (2501.01038v2, 16 Jul 2025, 'accepted by IEEE TWC'); the DOI is not printed in the file, so identity rests on the title. q4 counted from FLOPs-derived energy (formulas p. 11, ratios p. 12), reviewer to confirm. The PPO baseline is the proposed method without spiking networks, so q3 rests on DDPG, DQN, and the Random scheme.
